piezas.titulo: Clinical efficacy evaluation of combined central and peripheral repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for elbow flexor (biceps Brachii) spasticity and upper limb motor function after stroke
piezas.resumenOriginal: ObjectiveThis randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy and temporal dynamics of a combined central and peripheral magnetic stimulation protocol, combining central (M1) and peripheral (Erb’s point) stimulation with conventional rehabilitation, for post-stroke elbow flexor spasticity and motor function.MethodsOne hundred eligible stroke patients with upper limb spasticity were randomly allocated to Group A (n = 50) or Group B (n = 50). In a 6-week delayed-start design, Group A received active combined central and peripheral magnetic stimulation during weeks 1–3, while Group B received it during weeks 4–6. Both groups received concurrent conventional rehabilitation throughout. Primary outcomes included the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) for spasticity and the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) for motor function. Secondary neurophysiological outcomes comprised motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude and the root mean square (RMS) of biceps brachii electromyography. Assessments were performed at baseline, after 3-weeks and 6 weeks.ResultsA clear phase-specific effect was observed. At 3 weeks, Group A demonstrated significantly greater reduction in MAS scores (2(2, 3) vs. 3(2, 3), p < 0.001) and greater improvement in FMA-UE scores (22.2 ± 5.63 vs. 19.2 ± 5.53, p = 0.010) compared to Group B. Neurophysiologically, Group A showed an earlier reduction in RMS (20.14 ± 6.71 μV vs. 27.48 ± 7.29 μV, p < 0.001) and a transient decrease in contralesional MEP amplitude at 3 weeks. These intergroup differences narrowed at 6 weeks after Group B received the delayed intervention, suggesting that delayed active stimulation may also confer benefit, although spontaneous recovery and concurrent rehabilitation may have contributed to this convergence. Furthermore, the MEP elicitation rate in the affected hemisphere increased more substantially after combined central and peripheral magnetic stimulation treatment, suggesting a significant enhancement of cortical excitability in the affected hemisphere.ConclusionA combined central and peripheral rTMS protocol integrated with conventional rehabilitation is effective in alleviating elbow flexor spasticity and improving motor function after stroke. The delayed-start design supports that the observed benefits are attributable to the rTMS intervention, although residual placebo effects cannot be fully excluded. The effects are phase-specific, with motor improvement maintained at 6 weeks and a complex temporal pattern of spasticity reduction, likely mediated by modulating cortical excitability and spinal motor neuron pool activity.

piezas.titulo: Prevalence of chronic pain among U.S. children with neurodevelopmental disorders.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Introduction Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) affect up to 15% of children in the United States and are associated with co-occurring health challenges such as chronic pain, which can negatively affect development and quality of life. Increased risk of chronic pain in children with NDDs remains poorly understood; this study aimed to estimate chronic pain prevalence among children with NDDs and explore whether this association differs by sex. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of children participating in the 2022 to 2023 National Survey of Children's Health (age 3-17 years, n = 84,117). Neurodevelopmental disorders included attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder, autism, intellectual disability, speech disorder, Tourette syndrome, learning disability, and developmental delay. Chronic pain was defined as frequent or persistent pain in the past 12 months. Weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between NDDs and chronic pain, adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates. Results Overall, 18.7% (95% confidence interval: 18.2%-19.2%) of children had an NDD. Chronic pain prevalence was higher among children with NDDs than among those without (10.3% vs 5.2%, P P = 0.79). Conclusion Neurodevelopmental disorders affect 1 in 6 U.S. children and are associated with almost double the odds of chronic pain. This increased odds emphasizes the need for improved chronic pain recognition and management among children with NDDs. Future research should examine chronic pain in youth with NDDs, to improve assessment, management, and understanding of pain mechanisms.

piezas.titulo: Divergence in neurodivergent brains: mapping the relationship between developmental trajectories in functional connectivity and clinical outcomes
piezas.resumenOriginal: Brain network development differs between neurodivergent (ND) and neurotypical (NT) youth, but its developmental trajectory, and relationship to clinical outcomes, remains unclear. We examined age-related changes in functional network connectivity and clinical symptoms in 861 participants (5-21 years) from the Healthy Brain Network, including NT youth and those with Neurodevelopmental Disorders (NDDs) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). Functional connectivity during movie-watching was modeled using generalized additive models across eight large-scale networks to characterize nonlinear developmental trajectories. Divergence in connectivity profiles between ND and NT groups first emerged during late childhood and were largest during adolescence. Importantly, divergence in connectivity patterns followed a similar trajectory path, but preceded, divergence in clinical outcomes. These findings identify adolescence as a sensitive period when differences in patterns of brain activity and clinical differences become increasingly pronounced, highlighting a potential window for targeted intervention.
